blocks.text: The Open Container Initiative standardizes the image format, the runtime bundle, and the registry API, so images built by any tool run on any compliant runtime.

rows: Docker-built images run on Podman, containerd, CRI-O
runc, crun, gVisor, Kata are swappable
Docker Hub, GHCR, ECR, Harbor interoperate

items: Manifest: points to one config blob and an ordered list of layer blobs, all by sha256 digest.
Config: runtime defaults (Env, Entrypoint, Cmd, User, WorkingDir, ExposedPorts) and layer diff IDs.
Layers: tarballs of filesystem changes; deletions are "whiteout" files.
Image index (manifest list): one manifest per platform, enabling multi-arch tags.
Content addressing makes blobs verifiable and deduplicated across images and registries.

blocks.text: Registries also store OCI artifacts next to images: signatures, SBOMs, attestations, Helm charts.

Q: "Why does an image built with Docker run on Kubernetes without Docker?" A: "Because it's an OCI image: a standard manifest, config and layers. Any OCI-compliant runtime such as containerd or CRI-O can pull and run it."

items: Image = manifest + config + layers, all content-addressed.
Multi-arch works via an image index.
OCI means no tool lock-in for building or running.
